{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "Create a luxury fan-page / marketing website for a fictional contemporary artist named Aurelia Voss, inspired by the premium editorial feel and smooth browsing experience of Spotify artist pages, but for visual art instead of music. The website must be fully static and use only mock/sample content, no backend, no login, no database, no APIs.

# Project: Aurelia Voss — Official Fan Page

## Goal
Build a high-end static website that celebrates the artist, her collections, exhibitions, collectors, and visual universe. It should feel like a luxury digital magazine mixed with a modern artist fan hub. Think black, champagne gold, ivory, deep emerald, soft gradients, cinematic photography, elegant typography, and smooth parallax scrolling.

## Main Style Direction
- Luxury art fan-page
- Spotify-inspired layout language: hero profile section, featured works, collection cards, artist stats, playlist-like rows but for artworks/exhibitions
- Dark premium theme with gold accents
- Editorial, cinematic, elegant, expensive feeling
- Complex layout, not a simple one-page template
- Smooth scroll and parallax effects on hero images, floating frames, background textures, collection sections
- Mobile responsive but desktop should feel very polished
- Static only, sample text and placeholder images are fine

## Pages / Sections

### 1. Hero / Artist Profile Header
- Full-screen opening section
- Large artist portrait or abstract artwork background
- Artist name: Aurelia Voss
- Tagline: “Where silence becomes pigment”
- Verified-style label like “Featured Contemporary Artist” but do not use any real verification system
- Big CTA buttons:
  - Explore Collections
  - View Exhibition Timeline
- Spotify-like profile stats but adapted:
  - 1.8M global admirers
  - 42 signature works
  - 17 gallery features
  - 9 private collections
- Add parallax background movement while scrolling

### 2. Featured Masterpiece Section
- Large showcase card for one highlighted artwork
- Title: “Nocturne in Gold Leaf”
- Year, medium, dimensions, collection name
- Elegant descriptive paragraph
- Include a luxury frame effect around the artwork
- Add small metadata chips: Acrylic, Gold Leaf, Large Format, Private Collection
- Button: “Read the Story”

### 3. Artwork Collections
Create Spotify playlist style horizontal / grid sections, but for art collections:
- The Gilded Silence Collection
- Velvet Cities
- After Midnight Studies
- Botanical Shadows
- Letters to the Moon
Each card should include:
- Mock artwork image
- Collection title
- Short description
- Number of works
- Mood tags
- Hover effect with gold glow or soft scale

### 4. Fan Favorite Gallery
- Masonry-style or editorial grid gallery
- 10–12 sample artworks
- Each item should have artwork title, year, mood, and small fan reaction text
- Include static mock numbers like “24K saves” or “8.7K admirers” but clearly just display text, no live data
- Add a filter-looking UI row for All / Gold / Night / Portraits / Abstract, but it can be decorative/static or simple front-end filtering only, no backend

### 5. Artist Story
- Long editorial section about Aurelia Voss
- Split layout with text on one side and parallax image panels on the other
- Include timeline-style blocks:
  - 2016 — First private salon exhibition
  - 2019 — “Velvet Cities” series begins
  - 2022 — International gallery residency
  - 2026 — “Nocturne Archive” retrospective concept
- Use elegant pull quote: “I paint what the room remembers after everyone has left.”

### 6. Exhibition Timeline
- Premium timeline layout with cards
- Upcoming and past fictional exhibitions:
  - The Nocturne Archive — Paris
  - Gold Against Silence — Milan
  - Velvet Cities After Dark — London
  - Botanical Shadows — Lisbon
- Each card should include date, location, description, status badge
- No booking system, no ticket purchase, just static display

### 7. Collector Notes / Fan Wall
- Static testimonial-style section from fictional collectors, critics, and fans
- Cards should feel like luxury review snippets
- Example names can be fictional:
  - Maren L., private collector
  - Theo Armand, art critic
  - Elise Navarro, gallery curator
- Include quote marks, subtle borders, gold hover highlights

### 8. Visual Mood Board
- Create a parallax collage section with layered images/textures
- Include words like: Obsidian, Gold Leaf, Velvet, Moonlit Glass, Old Perfume, Rain on Marble
- Should feel immersive and artistic
- Use scroll animations if possible with CSS/JS only

### 9. Limited Prints Showcase
- Static product showcase style section for fictional art prints
- 3 pricing cards or product cards:
  - Collector Print
  - Museum Edition
  - Signature Archive Box
- Include mock prices, sizes, and features
- Important: no checkout, no payment, no cart, no backend. Just a “Join Interest List” style button that can scroll to contact section or be decorative.

### 10. Press / Editorial Mentions
- Static logo strip or article cards with fictional magazine names
- Examples:
  - LUXE CANVAS
  - MODERN SALON
  - ART NOIR REVIEW
  - THE GOLD ROOM JOURNAL
- Include short article headlines

### 11. Newsletter / Contact Style Footer
- Static fan signup section with an email field for visual only or front-end-only alert message
- No real submission or external service
- Include social-style links as placeholders
- Footer navigation:
  - Collections
  - Gallery
  - Story
  - Exhibitions
  - Prints

## Interaction Requirements
- Smooth parallax scrolling on hero, artwork panels, and mood board
- Sticky or floating navigation with active section feel
- Hover effects on cards
- Smooth anchor scrolling
- Animated reveal on scroll using CSS/JS only
- Optional decorative audio-player inspired bar at bottom like Spotify, but it must not play real music. It can show “Viewing: Nocturne in Gold Leaf” with a progress-style decorative line.

## Design Details
- Use luxury fonts: elegant serif for headings, clean sans-serif for UI
- Color palette:
  - Near black: #070707
  - Champagne gold: #D6B46A
  - Ivory: #F4EEE2
  - Deep emerald: #10251F
  - Warm gray: #8D8274
- Use glassmorphism only lightly
- Add subtle grain/noise texture if possible with CSS
- Large spacing, premium editorial rhythm
- Rounded corners should be subtle, not too playful
- Mobile layout must stack cleanly

## Deliverable
Build the complete static front-end website. React is fine, or plain HTML/CSS/JS is fine, but it must run as a static site with mock content only. No real APIs, no backend routes, no account system, no external data fetching, no database, no 3D/WebGL/canvas game. Please make it polished and production-looking, not just wireframes.",
 "judge": {
  "model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8",
  "model_sha": "94125d2bd83076b21eed33119525e29eaf3894f4",
  "request_model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8:novita",
  "provider": "novita",
  "pinned_on": "2026-10-09",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "rubric_id": "rva1:mean(visual,query,asset)"
 }
}

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
